title: Scenario 11: the printer that takes three minutes
task: The printer on 1/1/3 takes almost three minutes to get on every time it powers up, and the kiosk PC on 1/1/4, whose 802.1X client hangs halfway through, holds its port about as long. Plug both in and let the clock run with `sim wait` while `show port-access clients detail` says where each one is. Get the printer on in about 10 seconds without putting MAC auth first on the port, and make the kiosk's 802.1X attempt give up inside a minute. Re-authenticate both ports and time them again.
hints: `show port-access clients detail`: Status Authenticating, `dot1x - Authenticating, mac-auth - Not attempted`. The printer has no 802.1X client, so the port waits for an answer that never comes before it tries MAC auth.

`initial-auth-response-timeout 10` under `aaa authentication port-access dot1x authenticator` on 1/1/3 is how long the port waits for that first answer. On my bench the printer went from 165 s to about 10 s.

The kiosk does answer and then stalls, so that timer does nothing for it. `eapol-timeout 10` and `max-eapol-requests 1` under the same block on 1/1/4 took a stalled client from about 164 s to about 42 s on the lab switch.

`port-access reauthenticate interface 1/1/3` starts a fresh attempt so you can time it, then `sim wait 15`. Putting `auth-precedence mac-auth dot1x` on the port is faster still, but then a MAC-auth accept ends it and a laptop on that port never tries 802.1X.

checks.desc: The printer's port gives up on 802.1X in 15 s or less, and still tries 802.1X first
The kiosk's port gives up on its stalled 802.1X inside a minute
The printer is on in role PRINTERS by MAC auth
The kiosk got on in role KIOSK once 802.1X gave up
